title: A sandboxed agent in a worktree can record relay-run steps
lead: A relay role whose sandbox may write only inside its slice worktree can still record `relay-run step` and `end`, so the shared ledger introduced by s298 does not drop the steps of sandboxed vendors.
findings_note: s314 Codex relay 2026-10-16: review and gate ledger entries omitted after sandbox blocks
boundary: **Not in this slice:** deleting events from local files after absorbing them; changing where an unsandboxed writer appends.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
On 2026-10-16 a Codex relay ran s314 (orchestrator and implementer gpt-6.1-sol). Its report said: "Review/gate ledger entries were omitted after sandbox blocks". The shared ledger shows only steps 1 and 2. Since s298 the ledger in a git repo is `<git common dir>/slicer/relay-runs.jsonl`, and its lock file sits beside it (`relayrun.append`, `src/slicer/relayrun.py:378`; `ops.ledger_lock`, `src/slicer/ops.py:2950`). For a linked worktree, the common dir is the main checkout's `.git/`, outside the worktree. A workspace-write sandbox (Codex's default) refuses writes there, so every `relay-run step` from inside the sandbox fails. Before s298, the ledger was the worktree's own `.slicer/relay-runs.jsonl`, which the sandbox allows. The board and `relay-run list` then show a run with missing rounds, which is the problem the ledger exists to prevent.

**Decision (owner, 2026-10-16): fall back per write, absorb on end.**
- When opening the shared ledger or its lock fails with a permission error, the event goes to this checkout's `.slicer/relay-runs.jsonl` under the project lock, with one stderr line naming both paths.
- The fallback never edits `.slicer/.gitignore`. It relies on the ignore rule s300 settles, so a sandboxed write cannot put a tracked change into the slice's commit.
- `list_runs` and `_open_run` fold a run's events from every ledger they read into one run, ordered by time. A begin in the shared ledger plus steps in a worktree's file make one run.
- When `relay-run end` can write the shared ledger, it first copies that run's events from every local fallback file it reads (this checkout and its siblings) into the shared ledger. The fold drops duplicates, so `git worktree remove` cannot lose them afterwards. The outer session, which ends runs, can always write there.
- The docs add the alternative of making `<main>/.git/slicer` a writable root for a sandboxed vendor (Codex `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots`), which avoids the fallback altogether.

The owner rejected docs alone and a ledger-path setting: each needs per-setup configuration, and getting it wrong silently loses steps.

sections.heading: Files
Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_RelayRunStep_SharedLedgerReadOnly_FallsBackToLocalAndWarns`
- `test_RelayRunStep_Fallback_DoesNotEditGitignore`
- `test_RelayRunList_RunSpansSharedAndLocal_OneRunAllSteps`
- `test_RelayRunList_EventsAcrossFiles_OrderedByTimeNoDuplicates`
- `test_RelayRunEnd_AbsorbsLocalStepsIntoShared`: after `end`, removing the worktree that held the fallback steps leaves every step listed.
- `test_RelayRunEnd_SharedStillReadOnly_EndsLocallyWithoutAbsorbing`

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Fallback writes, then the cross-file fold, then absorb-on-end; mutation-check (no fallback; fold per file; skip the absorb; edit `.gitignore` again).
3. Docs and CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
